# Mahāhatthipadopama Sutta (MN 28 (PTS MN i 184))

**ID:** MN 28 (PTS MN i 184)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Mahāhatthipadopama Sutta
**PTS:** MN i 184
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāhatthipadopama Sutta* ("The Longer Simile of the Elephant’s Footprint", MN 28) is the twenty-eighth discourse in the *Majjhimanikāya* [Buswell & Lopez 2014]. Delivered by the Venerable Sāriputta, its governing pedagogical framework is the simile that just as the footprints of all living beings fit within that of an elephant, so all wholesome states and teachings are subsumed under the Four Noble Truths [Buswell & Lopez 2014; Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. Sāriputta develops this by examining the truth of suffering in terms of the five aggregates of clinging (*upādānakkhandha*), focusing extensively on material form (*rūpa*) divided into the four primary elements (*mahābhūta*): earth, water, fire, and wind [Buswell & Lopez 2014; Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Radich 2007]. Each element is contemplated across its internal (bodily) and external manifestations, demonstrating their impermanence and insubstantiality to cultivate non-attachment and eliminate self-identification [Radich 2007; Segall 2003; Wen, Sukkhavipassaka]. The text also preserves the well-known dictum that seeing dependent origination (*paṭiccasamuppāda*) is equivalent to seeing the Dhamma [IABU 2012; Radich 2007].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: MA 30 象跡喻
- Passage-level parallels: MN 21 (PTS MN i 122) Kakacūpama Sutta
- Mentioned in: Kv 22.8 Khaṇikakathā

**Sources**

- [Buswell & Lopez 2014] Robert E. Buswell Jr. & Donald S. Lopez Jr., The Princeton Dictionary of Buddhism (2014) — Entry on Mahāhatthipadopamasutta detailing the setting, Sāriputta, elephant footprint simile, four truths, elements, and Chinese titles.
- [Nyanaponika et al. 2003] Nyanaponika Thera, Hellmuth Hecker, and Bhikkhu Bodhi, Great Disciples of the Buddha: Their Lives, Their Works, Their Legacy (2003) — Analysis of Sāriputta's analytical exposition, structure of the Four Noble Truths, suffering, and aggregates in MN 28.
- [Radich 2007] Michael David Radich, The Somatics of Liberation: Ideas about Embodiment in Buddhism from Its Origins to the Fifth Century C.E. (2007) — Detailed doctrinal analysis of MN 28 moving from truths to skandhas, internal/external elements, and the seeing of dependent origination/Dhamma.
- [Wen, Sukkhavipassaka] Tzungkuen Wen, A Study of Sukkhavipassaka in Pali Buddhism — Comparison of elements in MN 28, MN 62, and MN 140, the Visuddhimagga treatment, and differences in element definitions with MĀ 30.
- [Meisig 2010] Konrad Meisig, Translating Buddhist Chinese: Problems and Prospects (2010) — Identification of MN 28 as the Pali parallel to MĀ 30.
- [IABU 2012] Buddhist Philosophy and Meditation Practice, 2nd IABU Conference (2012) — Citations of MN 28 regarding dependent origination, Four Noble Truths, and Right Resolve.
- [Berkwitz 2013] Stephen C. Berkwitz, Buddhist Poetry and Colonialism: Alagiyavanna and the Portuguese in Sri Lanka (2013) — References to psychic and physical elements in MN 28 and translation by Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi.
- [Segall 2003] Seth Robert Segall (ed.), Encountering Buddhism: Western Psychology and Buddhist Teachings (2003) — Glossary summary of MN 28 on materiality and nonself, and role in explaining aggregates.
- [Anālayo 2019] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Mindfulness of Breathing: A Practice Guide and Translations (2019) — Discussion of the internal wind element listing in MN 28.
